commits.author: Zachary Whitley
commits.message:
fix(bindgen): 6 fixes across parser + codegen + CLI


- CodeGenerator.generate() merges per-file BindgenModels before code
  emission. Previously each WIT file's javaCodeGenerator invocation
  emitted its own <RuntimeProvider>.java, and the last write silently
  overwrote earlier ones — killing SPI dispatchers for every interface

- BindgenCli.validateSources uses Files.walk instead of listFiles so
  `-w wit/deps` picks up every .wit under the tree. Combined with the
  merge fix, multi-file WIT packages resolve intra-package `use` refs
  correctly. Test: BindgenCliTest.shouldRecursivelyExpandDirectorySource.

- WitParser accepts stream<T> and future<T>: coerces to list<T> and
  option<T> respectively with a WARNING log rather than throwing
  BindgenException. Async component-model types are not modeled but the
  surrounding file stays parseable. Test: WitParserTest.asyncTypesCoerced.

- JavaCodeGenerator.mapType gains a TUPLE arm that recursively maps
  each element (was defaulting to embedding raw WIT text as a Java
  type name). TypeMappingRegistry.mapTuple emits parameterised
  headers shape) and parameterised TupleN placeholder otherwise. Test:
  NestedContainerFieldTest.

- ImplementationCodeGenerator passes parametrised Class<?>/Class<T>
  (not raw Class) to JavaPoet for WasmBindingProvider.supports/create
  overrides, resolving name-clash errors under erasure. Marshalling
  strategy branches on WIT element kind for list<T> params: real unbox
  loop for list<u8>/list<s8>, honest TODO-fallback for other elements.
  Tests: ImplementationCodeGeneratorBugsTest.

- MarshallingStrategy.liftReturn returns Optional<CodeBlock>; caller
  emits UnsupportedOperationException throw when Optional is empty
  (mirrors resultDispatch fallback). JavaCodeGenerator.shouldSkipInterface
  filters interface-and-record-with-same-name pairs (per ADR pattern
  in provider-manifest.wit) skipping emission with a warning rather
  than colliding on class name. Tests: InterfaceNestedTypeCollisionTest.

Suite: 458 -> 510 tests, all pass. Full 18-module install green.

commits.author: Zachary Whitley
commits.message:
feat(provider): caller-scoped externImports wire-through

F-Wasmtime4j-Caller-Scoped-Instantiate-Extern-Imports r.2. Replaces
WasmtimeCallerAdapter.instantiate's blanket LinkingException on
externImports with a per-def routing loop:

- MemoryImport / TableImport whose source is a WasmtimeMemoryAdapter /
  WasmtimeTableAdapter carrying a callerExportName (minted by
  Caller.getMemory/getTable in a callback frame) → route to the new
  caller-scoped linkerDefineMemoryFromExport / TableFromExport by-name
  native path (avoids registry-handle mismatch).

- MemoryImport / TableImport / GlobalImport with outer-scoped externs
  → route to linkerDefineMemory / Table / Global handle-based path.

- FunctionImport remains unsupported (waits on Function.unwrap).

WasmtimeMemoryAdapter / WasmtimeTableAdapter gain an optional
callerExportName field to signal caller-scoped origin; getMemory /
getTable on WasmtimeCallerAdapter set it.

commits.author: Zachary Whitley
commits.message:
test(wasmtime-provider): restrict caller-aware test callback to scoped ops only

Initial test called t.size() from inside the caller callback via the
regular WasmtimeTableAdapter delegate; that path routes through
WasmTable.getSize which acquires the store lock, and inside a live
caller-borrow the JniTable native SIGSEGVs — witnessed via hs_err
crash at libwasmtime4j.dylib Table::size + JniTable_nativeGetSize.

Callback now:
- reads args via observedArg, not size()
- calls only caller.growTable (borrow-safe scoped path)

Also swaps the run(param i32) wasm to a run() no-param variant that
calls trigger_grow with an inline i32.const 1 — sidesteps the
pre-existing WasmtimeFunctionAdapter I_V fast-path bug where
(i32) -> () signatures route through callVoid() and drop the arg
("Parameter validation failed for function 'run'"). Wasm bytes
regenerated (88 -> 91 bytes).

Assertions unchanged: pre/post-callback table size, growTable return
value, use-after-return IllegalStateException from wasmtime4j r.2
generation counter.

commits.author: Zachary Whitley
commits.message:
test(wasmtime-provider): caller-aware host function + scoped growTable from callback

Hand-authored 88-byte wasm module imports env.trigger_grow, exports a
1-slot funcref table + memory, and calls trigger_grow(1) from run().
Test registers trigger_grow as a CallerAwareHostFunction whose
callback resolves the caller's table export via caller.getTable("table")
then grows it by 1 via caller.growTable — the borrow-safe scoped path
routed through the wasmtime4j r.2 caller handle. Asserts:

- pre-grow size observed inside the callback is 1
- growTable return value is the previous size (1)
- post-callback instance.table("table").size() is 2
- retained Caller handle used after callback return throws
  IllegalStateException with a caller-generation message
  (proves wasmtime4j's use-after-return generation counter propagates
  through the api-layer adapter unchanged)

Kept in the WasmtimeLinkingContextExternImportsTest style — inline
hand-authored wasm bytes so the test needs no build-time toolchain.

commits.author: Zachary Whitley
commits.message:
feat(wasmtime-provider): WasmtimeModuleAdapter consumes callerAwareHostFunctions from LinkingContext

Extends WasmtimeModuleAdapter.instantiate(LinkingContext) to consume
the new LinkingContext.callerAwareHostFunctions() list added at
r.1-1. Each CallerAwareHostFunctionDefinition is registered on the
linker as a wasmtime4j CallerAwareHostFunction — the subclass of
HostFunction whose execute runs with the native Caller available via
the CallerContextProvider SPI wired at wasmtime4j r.2. The native
caller is wrapped in a WasmtimeCallerAdapter and handed to the user's
CallerAwareHostFunction implementation.

Also adds a caller-scoped factory (WasmtimeModuleAdapter.callerScoped)
so WasmtimeCallerAdapter.compileModule can return a Module wrapper
that has no owning store; its own instantiate() paths throw with a
clear message pointing at Caller.instantiate. Extracts
defineHostFunctions to a package-private static helper for reuse
from WasmtimeCallerAdapter and adds a package-private nativeModule()
accessor for the caller-scoped instantiate bridge.

commits.author: Zachary Whitley
commits.message:
feat(wasmtime-provider): WasmtimeCallerAdapter — wraps wasmtime4j Caller<T> as api Caller<T>

Bridges wasmtime4j's caller-scoped host-callback handle
(ai.tegmentum.wasmtime4j.func.Caller) into the webassembly4j api
Caller<T> interface added at r.1-1. Delegates each api method to the
underlying wasmtime4j Caller, wrapping/unwrapping types via existing
Wasmtime{Memory,Table,Function,Global,Instance}Adapter classes.

For instantiate(Module, LinkingContext), reconciles the api signature
against wasmtime4j's Caller.instantiate(InstancePre) by building a
transient linker from the caller's engine, calling instantiatePre on
it, then routing the pre through the caller's borrow-safe scoped
entrypoint. externImports are rejected at this path — they require a
live store binding that wasmtime4j's Caller does not expose.

compileModule returns a caller-scoped Module wrapper that has no
owning store; instantiation must go through Caller.instantiate.

commits.author: Zachary Whitley
commits.message:
feat(api): add Caller<T> + CallerAwareHostFunction<T> interfaces + LinkingContext plumbing

Charter r.1-1. Engine-agnostic exposure of the wasmtime4j r.2 / r.2.b
Caller<T> scoped-mutation pattern.

- Caller<T>: 10 scoped methods (data, getMemory, getTable, getFunction,
  getGlobal, compileModule, instantiate, growTable, setTableElement,
  growMemory, unwrap).
- CallerAwareHostFunction<T>: @FunctionalInterface — Object[] execute(
  Caller<T>, Object...).
- CallerAwareHostFunctionDefinition: parallel to HostFunctionDefinition
  but wraps CallerAwareHostFunction.
- LinkingContext.callerAwareHostFunctions(): default returns empty list;
  providers that do not support the pattern inherit safe no-op behavior.
- DefaultLinkingContext.Builder.addCallerAwareHostFunction(...): two
  overloads matching addHostFunction shape.

commits.message:
feat(api,wasmtime-provider): add Engine.loadModule(byte[], Instance) cross-module store sharing

F-Webassembly4j-Cross-Module-Store-Sharing r.1. Adds default-throwing overload
Engine.loadModule(byte[] bytes, Instance shareStoreWith) so consumers can load
a related module against an existing instance's store — required for any
composition pattern where the new module imports memory/table/global exports
of the shared instance (JIT install, plugin loading, incremental linking,
multi-module workflows).

wasmtime4j-provider implements: unwraps shareStoreWith to native Instance,
extracts its Store via getStore(), reuses the store when constructing the
new WasmtimeModuleAdapter (which already accepted an explicit Store — no
refactor needed).

Non-wasmtime providers inherit UnsupportedOperationException default.

Disciplined per operator gate: cross-module store sharing is a general
Wasm-embedding pattern already used internally by wasmtime4j-provider's
own tests via ((WasmtimeModuleAdapter) module).store() escape. This surfaces
the capability at the api layer.

Compile clean. Tests to follow in a separate commit.

commits.message:
feat(api,wasmtime-provider): Table interface completion (charter r.1 close)

Closes r.1 of the F-Webassembly4j-Table-Interface-Completion charter.

Interface (webassembly4j-api):
  - Adds default-throwing OptionalInt maxSize(), Object get(int),
    void set(int, Object), int grow(int, Object) to Table.

    graalwasm4j-provider, wasm3-provider, endive4j-provider remain

  - maxSize maps native -1 (unbounded) to OptionalInt.empty().

Tests (wasmtime4j-provider):

    size and IOOBE contract (9 tests, all pass on JNI backend).

-Dskip.rust.build=true -Dtest='!JavaToWasmRoundTripTest,!WasmtimeCallableResourceTest'

commits.author: Zachary Whitley
commits.message:
test(wasmtime-provider): cover shared-import wiring via typed ExternImportDefinition

WasmtimeLinkingContextExternImportsTest exercises:

  - api-layer builder collects all four typed variants; ordering preserved
  - api-layer accepts a pre-built ExternImportDefinition via addExternImport
  - default LinkingContext.externImports() is empty
  - end-to-end MemoryImport wired on the module's own native store; host
    write is observable from the guest via the exported load_i32
  - end-to-end TableImport wired on the same store; instantiate succeeds
    and the api-layer table size flows through
  - end-to-end GlobalImport wired on the same store; guest bump is
    observable on the host handle and vice versa
  - FunctionImport raises UnsupportedOperationException with the variant
    kind and (moduleName, name) coordinates in the message
  - MemoryImport with a memory that unwrap-fails raises LinkingException
    naming the (moduleName, name) pair and identifying the cause

The three end-to-end tests reach through the package-private
WasmtimeModuleAdapter.store() accessor to construct WasmMemory / WasmTable
/ WasmGlobal on the module's own native store — the wasmtime constraint is
that extern imports must live on the same Store as the module being
instantiated. That accessor already existed; no adapter API change is
needed for these tests.

Note: bump in IMPORT_GLOBAL_MODULE is 0-arg to sidestep a pre-existing
i32-in/void-out fast-path shortcut in WasmtimeFunctionAdapter (out of scope
for this charter).

Refs: f-webassembly4j-linkingcontext-imports-wiring-fix-charter-2026-07-26

commits.author: Zachary Whitley
commits.message:
fix(wasmtime-provider): translate native Table bounds errors to IOOBE

The api-layer Table contract (webassembly4j-api) promises
IndexOutOfBoundsException from get(int) and set(int, Object) when
index >= size(). The underlying ai.tegmentum.wasmtime4j.jni.JniTable
implementation surfaces out-of-bounds access as a bare RuntimeException
wrapping a WasmRuntimeException, and negative indices come out as
IllegalArgumentException (Validation.requireNonNegative).

Neither shape matches the contract, so the adapter now bounds-checks the
index against nativeTable.getSize() before delegating; failures raise
IndexOutOfBoundsException with a descriptive message. The delegating
call itself is unchanged.

Fixes the getOutOfBoundsThrows / setOutOfBoundsThrows cases in
WasmtimeTableAdapterTest introduced by the preceding commit.

commits.author: Zachary Whitley
commits.message:
feat(wasmtime-provider): consume LinkingContext.externImports for shared-import wiring

WasmtimeModuleAdapter.instantiate(LinkingContext) now processes each
ExternImportDefinition:

  - MemoryImport unwraps to WasmMemory and calls Linker.defineMemory
  - TableImport  unwraps to WasmTable  and calls Linker.defineTable
  - GlobalImport unwraps to WasmGlobal and calls Linker.defineGlobal
  - FunctionImport is not yet supported — throws UnsupportedOperationException
    with a clear message pointing at addHostFunction; wiring blocked on a
    Function.unwrap(Class) accessor scheduled for a follow-up charter

The empty-list fast-path is preserved: when hostFunctions, wasiContext, and
externImports are all empty, the adapter delegates to instantiate() as
before so today's callers see no behaviour change.

An unwrap that hands back Optional.empty (e.g. because the value came from
a different provider) raises LinkingException with the (moduleName, name)
coordinates identified.

Refs: f-webassembly4j-linkingcontext-imports-wiring-fix-charter-2026-07-26

commits.author: Zachary Whitley
commits.message:
feat(api): add typed extern-import builder methods; deprecate untyped addImport

DefaultLinkingContext.Builder grows:

  - addMemoryImport(moduleName, name, Memory)
  - addTableImport (moduleName, name, Table)
  - addGlobalImport(moduleName, name, Global)
  - addFunctionImport(moduleName, name, Function)
  - addExternImport(ExternImportDefinition)  // pre-built variant

DefaultLinkingContext now implements
LinkingContext.externImports() by handing back an unmodifiable snapshot of
the builder-collected list.

Builder.addImport(String, Object) is marked @Deprecated — the call has
always been a no-op with respect to instantiation because the imports map
was never exposed through the LinkingContext interface. The method is kept
functional (still writes to the private map) so existing call-sites compile
with only a warning.

Refs: f-webassembly4j-linkingcontext-imports-wiring-fix-charter-2026-07-26

commits.author: Zachary Whitley
commits.message:

Default method returns an empty list so all existing LinkingContext

Refs: f-webassembly4j-linkingcontext-imports-wiring-fix-charter-2026-07-26

commits.author: Zachary Whitley
commits.message:
feat(api): add ExternImportDefinition types for typed extern-imports

Introduces a typed replacement for the untyped
DefaultLinkingContext.Builder.addImport(String, Object) call — which was
never reachable through the LinkingContext interface, so had no effect. The
new hierarchy carries both the (moduleName, name) pair that Wasm imports
require and the target-typed value that a provider can hand to its native
linker:

  ExternImportDefinition (interface)
    - MemoryImport(moduleName, name, Memory)
    - TableImport (moduleName, name, Table)
    - GlobalImport(moduleName, name, Global)
    - FunctionImport(moduleName, name, Function)

Because the webassembly4j-api module targets Java 8, the interface is not
`sealed` and the variants are plain final classes rather than records;
callers should still treat the set of implementations as closed and dispatch
via `instanceof`.

Only the value types land here — the LinkingContext interface accessor and
the wasmtime provider wiring follow in the next commits.

Refs: f-webassembly4j-linkingcontext-imports-wiring-fix-charter-2026-07-26

commits.author: Zachary Whitley
commits.message:
feat(api): add spec-standard Table operations (maxSize/get/set/grow)

Extends ai.tegmentum.webassembly4j.api.Table with four WebAssembly-spec
operations so api-layer consumers can perform basic dynamic table
management without dropping through unwrap():

- OptionalInt maxSize() maps to table.type().max
- Object get(int) maps to table.get
- void set(int, Object) maps to table.set
- int grow(int, Object) maps to table.grow (returns -1 on failure)

All four are declared as default methods that throw
UnsupportedOperationException so unchanged provider adapters
(wamr4j-provider, graalwasm4j-provider, wasm3-provider,
endive4j-provider) continue to compile without modification. Providers
opt in by overriding.

The Object element type is provider-specific until a spec-based Ref
abstraction lands (deferred). For funcref-typed tables, null denotes an
uninitialized slot.

No removals, no signature changes; existing consumers are unaffected.
